Keretsky Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zakarpattia Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Jews are believed to have arrived in Keretsky in the first half of the 19th century, growing from 9 people in 1840–51 to 252 by 1921 under Czechoslovakian rule, working as tradesmen and farmers. Following the March 1939 Hungarian occupation, Jews were persecuted and forced out of their occupations; by 1941, 327 Jews lived in Keretsky. Some were drafted into forced labor battalions or sent to the Eastern Front, where most perished. In August 1941, Jews without Hungarian citizenship were expelled to Nazi-occupied Kamianets-Podilskyi and murdered, and the remaining Jews of Keretsky were deported to Auschwitz in mid-May 1944.
